items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...it made me think — you probably are aware that both Milt Hinton and Joe Wilder carried a camera wherever they went.

ctx.x: and he couldn’t get back into the building. I don’t know if he forgot his ID or somebody wouldn’t let him back into the building. So it’s 11:59 or something and the band is about to go on and Bryan Ferry said, “I need that conga part, I need the percussion part.” And Sammy had a set-up of five drums, five congas. And I’d been digging him all week. So he said, “Can you play the conga part?” And I said uhhh sure. So I played this conga part and literally ten seconds before air I spotted Steve Jordan in the audience…

Let me talk about — I went to your website that was just for your visual art and I scrolled — it said sketch books. And I scrolled down and I said you have almost as many sketch books as you do LP credits. It’s a great idea. And it made me think — you probably are aware that both Milt Hinton and Joe Wilder carried a camera wherever they went. And they have just these kinds of pictures that no one else would get. And I was wondering, with all the — this question I have found the answer to — how did you find time…

Absolutely. I have a little Winsor Newton portable watercolor set that fits in with my cymbals and stick bag and I have a sketch book always. And there’s often downtime, you know after the sound check or between takes sometimes or while the guitar players are overdubbing or — there is often a time where you want to stay focused, you don’t want to lose the momentum or the continuity of the session and I found that having a sketch book and drawing in between takes or in those downtime periods that often happen on a…
